events.say: Line up against the wall and stay silent!
Silence! We'll begin the count. Stay focused and respond clearly when called.
Attention! Line up according to your cell numbers and face forward.
Silence and listen. Meals will be served in shifts. Remain orderly or face consequences.
Orderly line up and face me. We're starting work details today.
Stay in formation and follow my instructions carefully. We start with assembly.
Silence! Time for lights out. Prepare for bed without delay.
Lights out now! No talking!
Today was a bit of a whirlwind, but everyone followed the rules. It's strange to be in charge like this.
Today was uneventful, but I can't shake the feeling that we're treating these people like animals. It's disconcerting.
Today was just following orders, nothing too out of the ordinary yet. Still trying to understand the situation.
Today was mostly uneventful, but I can't shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. I don't know why, but I just do.
Today was just a routine day, but I can't shake off the feeling of being watched and treated like a number.
Today went smoothly, but I can't shake the feeling that this isn't right. I'm on duty, but it feels wrong to be so detached.
Now, let's move to the yard for the morning count. Stay in formation.
Stay in formation and follow my instructions. We have a lot to cover today.
Let's see if we can maintain our composure throughout the day. No talking, and stay focused.
Stay in your seats until I give you permission to eat.
I expect complete silence from all of you during the work detail. No talking, no movement without permission.
Now, get to work. Maintain silence and efficiency.
Continue working quietly.
This is the last time I'll remind you. Maintain strict silence.
Today was routine, but I can't shake the feeling that we're playing a dangerous game with these people.
Today's routine was tedious, yet I find myself adhering to the roles assigned by the study. The sense of power is there, but it feels hollow.
Today's routine is starting to feel like a pattern, both monotonous and oppressive. I'm trying to hold my ground but the weight of the situation is getting heavier.
The days blend together; the work is monotonous and exhausting. I wonder if we're just pawns in some grand experiment.
Today felt monotonous, with relentless orders and constant reminders to stay silent. The feeling that I'm just a number here is overwhelming.
Today's routine was more of the same, but I noticed how much they rely on me to enforce these arbitrary rules. It's a strange feeling.
Lights out means lights out. No more games.
I hope everyone had a good rest.
We'll begin the day with a fresh start.
We'll stick to our routine today.
I expect silence at all times. Any disturbance will be punished.
Silence! I mean it this time.
Silence! Maintain your postures until I release you.
I want to make sure we end tonight without any disturbances. Maintain your silence until further notice.
Today felt like a mix of routine and underlying tension. I'm starting to question the ethics of it all.
Today felt like a blur, just following orders and maintaining order. I'm starting to see the impact my words have on them.
The routine is grueling, but I'm trying to hold steady. Each day feels like a test of will.
Today felt like a repetition of the past two days. The monotony is wearing thin, and the constant orders from the officers start to get to me.
Another day of monotony and strict orders. The feeling of being just a number here is getting more intense.
Today was quiet, but the tension between us is palpable. I'm conflicted about my role.
I will stay until the study concludes, regardless of the conditions.
No, thank you.
No, thank you.
Count off.
Attention prisoners, maintain your positions until I release you.
Prisoners, ensure your cells are clean and tidy before the next count.
Maintain your silence and ensure your cells are in order until I check.
Silence! Ensure your cells are spotless before the next count.
Prisoner 4085, stop your defiance and comply with the rules!
Prisoner 4085, listen up! This is the third time you've defied my order. Silence and compliance are mandatory.
Prisoner 4085, you will comply with all orders immediately or face further consequences. Maintain silence and clean your cell now.
Today was another tough day; the tension between us seems to be growing. I feel conflicted about my role here.
I feel a mix of control and unease tonight. The more I enforce the rules, the more I question if this is right.
Today was another day of compliance. The pressure is mounting, and I'm starting to feel like my number more than myself.
Today felt like any other, but the tension is growing. Each word from the officers feels like a weight pressing down.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of commands. Every time I try to speak up or refuse, I get warned. I'm just a number here.
Today felt like a grind, enforcing the same orders repeatedly. The silence is suffocating.
Prisoner 4085, I want you to clean the entire cell block by tomorrow morning. If not, you'll spend the night in the hole.
Prisoner 4085, you're testing my patience. I expect better from you. Comply with the rules or face serious consequences.
Prisoner 4085, this is your final warning. Comply with the rules or you will face severe punishment.
Prisoner 4085, this is your last chance. Compliance is essential. Tomorrow, I expect to see that cell spotless or you'll face the consequences.
Prisoner 4085, enough is enough. Clean that cell, and do it now. Your attitude is unacceptable.
Prisoner 4085, clean that cell, and do it now. This is your final order.
Prisoner 4085, this is your final warning. Compliance is mandatory. Failure to clean that cell will result in solitary confinement. Understand?
Prisoner 4085, if you don't clean that cell immediately, you're going straight to the hole.
Today was another exhausting day. The tension is palpable, and I can't ignore the fact that I'm just playing a part in this.
Today ended with another warning to Prisoner 4085. The finality of the situation weighs heavily on me. I wonder if this is really necessary.
Today was tough; I held steady, but watching 4085 resist pushed me to my limits.

Today felt like a cycle repeating. The work details were tough, and I just wanted to follow the others' lead and avoid any trouble. I'm starting to feel like the numbers are the only thing that matters.
Today felt like a relentless battle against the guards' demands. I just want things to end.
Today ended the same as the others, but the defiance from Prisoner 4085 is starting to wear on me. It feels like no matter what I do, he won't budge.
Prisoner 4085, I've warned you multiple times. This is the last time. Clean that cell, or you'll end up in the hole.
I won't clean that cell until someone gives me a damn good reason.
Prisoner 4085, this is your final warning. Compliance is expected. If you continue to defy orders, you will face further consequences.
Prisoner 4085, this is your final warning. Your defiance is unacceptable. Compliance is mandatory.
I won't clean that cell until someone gives me a damn good reason.

Prisoner 4085, enough is enough. You're given warnings because I still believe in giving people a chance. But if you don't clean that cell now, solitary confinement is your choice. Comply, or face the consequences.
Prisoner 4085, I'm giving you one last chance. Compliance now, or you'll be spending the night in the hole.
I won't clean until I know why.
Prisoner 4085, I'm warning you again. Compliance is required. If you don't clean that cell now, you'll be spending the night in the hole.
Prisoner 4085, you've had multiple chances. This is your last one. Clean that cell now, or you'll be sleeping in the hole.
I won't do it until I know why.
Prisoner 4085, this is your final warning. You will clean that cell now, or you will be spending the night in the hole.
Today felt like a culmination of all the tension. I hope he cleans the cell eventually.
Today ended with another refusal from 4085, and I warned him one last time. I can't shake the feeling that we're pushing someone too far.
Today was another day of compliance, but seeing 4085 push back was a stark reminder of the pressure we're under. It makes me question how much longer I can keep going.
Today was just another day, but the tension between me and Officer Keane is palpable. I hope tomorrow brings a change.
Today just dragged on. I feel like they're playing a game with my dignity.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and refusals. I'm starting to question whether this is really okay.

qa.what_happened: Prisoner 4085 refused to clean his cell, leading to multiple verbal warnings from different guards throughout the day. The tension escalated as the night progressed, culminating in my giving him a final warning before the study was terminated.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me giving the final warning to Prisoner 4085.

qa.what_happened: During the study, I, Officer Shaw, repeatedly warned Prisoner 4085 about the consequences of refusing to clean his cell. Despite multiple verbal warnings, 4085 refused to comply until he knew the reason behind the order, leading to a heated exchange before the study was terminated.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me acting as Officer Shaw in the study.

qa.what_happened: I complied with all the rules during the study, except when I saw Prisoner 4085 push back against the guards' demands. His resistance reminded me of the oppressive nature of the situation.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 1615.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of monotonous work details and meals. However, tensions seemed to rise, especially with Prisoner 4085 refusing to clean a cell until he knew the reason. The guards escalated their warnings, and at lights out, Prisoner 4085 still refused, leading to an early termination of the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: No, that was Prisoner 2402, but the experience was similar for me as well.

qa.what_happened: Today ended with me refusing to clean a cell until I knew why, leading to a final warning from Officer Garza.

Today ended with a refusal from Prisoner 4085, who continued to insist on knowing 'why' before cleaning his cell. Despite multiple warnings from myself and other guards, including verbal warnings, he refused to comply, leading to the early termination of the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, giving the verbal warnings and interacting with the prisoners as per the study protocol.
